paragraphs: Graph neural networks usually learn from the connections they receive without modeling why those connections exist. This paper makes edge formation part of representation learning. It describes a graph as arising from interactions within overlapping communities of nodes, so a node can participate in several communities that contribute to the observed connections.

The generative model combines community contributions through a logical OR: a connection can arise through any contributing community. The method then splits each observed edge into weighted contributions associated with different communities. These contributions define separate community-specific graph neural networks, allowing the model to process different patterns of interaction through different networks.

A variational inference framework learns the edge partition, the community-specific networks, and a predictor that combines their outputs for classification together. Evaluations on real-world graphs support the method's effectiveness for both node and whole-graph classification. The central contribution is to connect an explanation of how edges arise with the supervised task of learning features that distinguish classes.
neurips-2022-a-variational-edge-partitio.tldr: The model partitions graph edges into overlapping community contributions and learns community-specific networks jointly for classification.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning a large language model on limited data can make it fit the training examples too closely. Dropout addresses this problem by randomly removing some model activity during training. This paper examines how that idea interacts with self-attention, using attribution scores to assess which attention positions contribute to predictions.

The authors observe that removing positions with low attribution can accelerate training while increasing the risk of overfitting. Their proposed method, AD-DROP, instead randomly removes some high-attribution positions. This encourages the model to draw more on positions that previously contributed less, reducing its dependence on the attention positions it already relies on most heavily.

Because repeatedly removing influential positions could become excessive, the method alternates ordinary fine-tuning with AD-DROP through a cross-tuning strategy. Experiments across multiple benchmarks show consistent improvements over the evaluated baselines, and further analysis supports its role as a regularizer. The contribution is a targeted way to use dropout within attention, guided by measured contributions to predictions.
neurips-2022-ad-drop-attribution-driven-.tldr: AD-DROP reduces fine-tuning overfitting by selectively dropping influential attention positions and alternating this intervention with ordinary training.

paragraphs: Active learning selects which examples should receive labels, making the quality of each selection important when labeling is expensive. This paper studies selection with Gaussian processes. It focuses on the balance between bias and variance, which becomes particularly consequential when only a small amount of labeled data is available.

The approach represents uncertainty jointly over the Gaussian process length scale and noise term, the two hyperparameters used here to control that balance. It approximates their joint posterior and uses it to construct two acquisition functions, which score possible queries. Bayesian Query-by-Committee uses this uncertainty in a committee formulation; Query by Mixture of Gaussian Processes explicitly targets lower predictive variance.

Across six simulators, Bayesian Query-by-Committee obtains the best marginal likelihood on average, while the mixture-based method achieves the best predictive performance. These are distinct empirical outcomes for the two selection objectives. The findings support accounting for the bias-variance trade-off when choosing new labels, helping avoid expensive queries that contribute less to the learning task.
neurips-2022-bayesian-active-learning-wi.tldr: Two Gaussian-process acquisition functions use uncertainty over hyperparameters to improve active learning and reduce unnecessary labeling.

paragraphs: Personalized treatment-effect models estimate how the effect of a treatment varies between people. Flexible models can capture complicated patterns, but their predictions alone do not reveal which characteristics drive those differences. This paper evaluates whether such models identify the variables that determine different responses to treatment.

The authors use post-hoc feature importance methods to examine which inputs influence a trained model's predictions. They build a benchmarking environment around the recovery of predictive covariates: characteristics that determine treatment-effect differences. This introduces an interpretability-focused evaluation dimension, allowing models to be assessed for what they appear to have learned about treatment heterogeneity.

The environment varies challenges specific to treatment-effect estimation, including the balance of prognostic and predictive information, nonlinear potential outcomes, and different forms of confounding. These controlled changes reveal strengths and weaknesses across model types. The contribution is a way to investigate whether a model's influential features reflect the relevant treatment-response structure, knowledge that could matter when interpreting personalized estimates in settings such as medicine.
neurips-2022-benchmarking-heterogeneous-.tldr: This benchmark uses feature importance to assess whether treatment-effect models identify the characteristics that drive different treatment responses.

paragraphs: Self-supervised encoders produce vector representations that can support many downstream applications. When exposed through public APIs, those rich outputs also make the encoders vulnerable to copying. This paper proposes a dataset inference defense that uses an encoder owner's private training data to help attribute ownership of a suspected stolen model.

The proposed signal is a difference between representations of training and test examples. The authors' intuition is that a stolen encoder assigns higher representation log-likelihood to the original encoder's training data than to test data, whereas an independently trained encoder does not show that same pattern. Density estimation models provide the likelihood estimates used to investigate this distinction.

The paper also proposes evaluating copying fidelity and theft detection directly at the representation level. It uses mutual information and distance measurements, avoiding the need to choose downstream tasks for these evaluations. Experiments in vision support dataset inference as a promising defense direction. The contribution concerns detecting and attributing copying through a training-data signature, with the reported support coming from empirical evaluation.
neurips-2022-dataset-inference-for-self-.tldr: Dataset inference uses representation likelihoods on an owner's private training data to help identify stolen self-supervised encoders.

paragraphs: Self-supervised pretraining has motivated efforts to improve molecular representations learned by graph neural networks. This paper investigates how much those efforts help on small molecules. Its central finding is qualified: across many examined settings, self-supervised graph pretraining does not provide a statistically significant advantage over training without it.

The authors systematically vary pretraining objectives, data splits, input features, pretraining dataset sizes, and network architectures. This helps separate the contribution of pretraining from other choices that affect downstream accuracy. Additional supervised pretraining can produce noticeable improvements, but those gains may shrink when input features are richer or data splits are more balanced.

Hyperparameter choices can also affect downstream accuracy more than the choice of pretraining task, especially when downstream datasets are small. The paper further offers conjectures, supported by empirical evidence across pretraining datasets, that some pretraining methods may be insufficiently complex for small molecules. Together, the results make the value of pretraining a setting-dependent question and emphasize careful comparisons of the surrounding experimental choices.
neurips-2022-does-gnn-pretraining-help-m.tldr: Ablation studies find that molecular GNN pretraining often brings limited gains, with features, data splits, and hyperparameters strongly affecting its apparent value.

paragraphs: Cooperating agents can struggle when a shared goal requires many stages of action. They must divide work, coordinate their behavior, and make progress through a long plan. E-MAPP addresses these difficulties by guiding reinforcement learning with programs designed to express work that can be carried out in parallel.

The framework uses both the structure of a parallel program and the meaning of its operations. Program structure supplies information about the organization of a task, while program semantics guide cooperative behavior. A task allocator improves time efficiency by distributing work among agents. Together, these components support goals requiring planning across more than ten stages.

The authors evaluate E-MAPP on challenging cooperative tasks in the Overcooked environment. They report large improvements over strong baselines in completion rate, time efficiency, and zero-shot generalization. These findings support parallel programs as useful guidance for the tested long-horizon tasks: the program gives agents an explicit organization for cooperation, while reinforcement learning supplies the behaviors needed to carry it out.
neurips-2022-e-mapp-efficient-multi-agen.tldr: E-MAPP uses parallel programs and task allocation to help multiple reinforcement-learning agents coordinate on long, multistage tasks.

paragraphs: Variational autoencoders learn by maximizing a lower bound on data log-likelihood, leaving a gap between the training objective and exact likelihood. This paper asks whether that gap helps explain their useful representations. The puzzle is that unregularized maximum likelihood alone cannot invert the data-generating process, yet VAEs often recover meaningful latent factors.

The analysis studies nonlinear VAEs in the limit of nearly deterministic decoders. In this regime, the authors prove that the optimal encoder approximately reverses the decoder. Using this self-consistency result, they show that the training objective approaches a regularized log-likelihood, giving the gap a specific role in shaping the learned representation.

The resulting bias favors decoders whose Jacobian columns are orthogonal, the structure associated with independent mechanism analysis. This can help recover the true latent factors. Experiments on synthetic and image data demonstrate recovery when the data-generating process satisfies the IMA assumption. The argument therefore ties representation recovery to both a particular theoretical regime and a stated structural assumption.
neurips-2022-embrace-the-gap-vaes-perfor.tldr: For nearly deterministic decoders, the VAE objective introduces a structural bias that helps recover latent factors when the IMA assumption holds.

paragraphs: Image compression balances the number of bits used against the distortion introduced into the reconstructed image. Neural compression can perform well on this trade-off, but often requires a separate encoder-decoder pair for each operating point. This paper proposes Code Editing to make a compression model usable across a wider range of requirements.

The method combines semi-amortized inference with adaptive quantization. Its central idea is to adjust the image code and its quantization, giving compression behavior more flexibility within a single decoding setup. This addresses the deployment burden of maintaining multiple dedicated models and the limited flexibility of the conditional coding approaches discussed in the paper.

Experiments show that Code Editing surpasses the evaluated variable-rate methods. The same decoder can also support region-of-interest coding and trade-offs among multiple distortion objectives, extending control beyond overall bitrate. The authors state compatibility with neural compression methods that have differentiable decoders, including existing pretrained models. That compatibility condition is central to the method's proposed usefulness as an adaptation of already trained compression systems.
neurips-2022-flexible-neural-image-compr.tldr: Code Editing adapts image codes and quantization to support variable bitrate and other compression trade-offs with a single differentiable decoder.

paragraphs: A robot may need more than the words of an instruction to understand what a person wants. HandMeThat evaluates instruction following when meaning depends on physical context, such as object states and relationships, and social context, such as the person's previous actions and goals. Resolving ambiguity is therefore part of the task itself.

The benchmark contains 10,000 episodes of human-robot interaction. In each episode, the robot observes a sequence of human actions directed toward an internal goal. The person then gives an instruction, and the robot must act to accomplish the requested subgoal. The paper presents a textual interface, through which the robot issues commands to a virtual environment.

This setup connects interpreting language with understanding an ongoing activity and planning appropriate actions. The evaluated baseline models include offline and online reinforcement learning algorithms, both of which perform poorly on the benchmark. Those results indicate substantial room for improvement on these tasks and motivate studying physical and social context together when evaluating human-robot communication.
neurips-2022-handmethat-human-robot-comm.tldr: HandMeThat benchmarks whether robots can resolve ambiguous instructions using object information and the context of a person's actions and goals.

paragraphs: Matrix completion reconstructs a low-rank matrix from only some of its entries, a task used in recommendation and other applications. Sending those entries to a server creates privacy concerns. This paper proposes an encryption scheme and completion procedure that let the server perform the reconstruction on encrypted data.

The key mathematical property connects encrypted computation with the intended plaintext result: decrypting the recovered encrypted matrix yields the target complete matrix. The authors prove this homomorphism property and also establish an epsilon-delta differential privacy guarantee. These results address both whether the encrypted procedure produces the desired answer and the stated privacy behavior of the scheme.

At a similar level of privacy guarantee, the paper replaces a previously known nonzero error bound with exact recovery, at the cost of requiring more observed samples. Experiments on numerical and real-world data show accurate encrypted-domain recovery using nuclear-norm minimization and alternating minimization. The contribution combines encrypted computation with recovery guarantees while making the additional sample requirement an explicit part of the trade-off.
neurips-2022-homomorphic-matrix-completi.tldr: The paper enables low-rank matrix completion on encrypted data, proving privacy and exact-recovery properties with an increased sample requirement.

paragraphs: Zero-shot image classification needs information about classes for which training images are unavailable. Human-written attribute labels are costly to scale, while embeddings of class names may fail to capture visual similarity. I2DFormer uses online documents as a richer source of class descriptions, drawing on their potentially useful visual information.

The framework jointly encodes images and documents into a shared representation space. Its cross-modal attention module learns interactions between individual image patches and document words. This fine-grained alignment helps extract visually discriminative words from documents containing irrelevant material, producing document representations that reflect visual relationships between classes.

The same alignment also lets the model associate relevant words with particular image regions, making the relationship between text and image more interpretable. On three public datasets, I2DFormer significantly outperforms previous unsupervised semantic embeddings in both zero-shot and generalized zero-shot settings. Qualitative results illustrate word-to-region grounding. The contribution links stronger class descriptions with a mechanism for identifying which parts of those descriptions correspond to visible content.
neurips-2022-i2dformer-learning-image-to.tldr: I2DFormer aligns image patches with document words to learn visually useful class descriptions for zero-shot image classification.

paragraphs: Feature distillation trains a student network using internal representations from a teacher. This paper investigates the projector that connects their features, a component whose role extends beyond matching feature dimensions. The authors observe that a projector can benefit the student even when teacher and student representations already have the same size.

Their explanation treats direct feature distillation as two simultaneous tasks: learning features useful for classification and matching the teacher's feature distribution. They hypothesize, and provide empirical support, that direct matching can make the student overfit the teacher's representations despite differences in architecture and initialization. That can degrade the features the student ultimately uses for classification.

A projector separates these demands, allowing the student's backbone to focus more on discriminative feature extraction while receiving teacher guidance through the projection. Motivated by that effect, the authors propose using an ensemble of projectors to further improve student features. Experiments across multiple datasets and teacher-student pairs support the method's effectiveness, alongside the proposed explanation for why projectors help.
neurips-2022-improved-feature-distillati.tldr: An ensemble of feature projectors improves distillation by helping separate teacher-feature matching from the student's classification feature learning.

paragraphs: Multi-task learning trains one model against several task objectives. A simple approach adds their losses and minimizes the total, a method called unitary scalarization. This paper revisits that approach after research proposing specialized optimizers to address difficulties attributed to learning multiple tasks together.

Many specialized methods require a separate gradient for each task, increasing memory use, runtime, and implementation effort. The authors compare these methods with summed-loss training strengthened by standard regularization and stabilization techniques from single-task learning. In the supervised and reinforcement learning settings studied, this combination matches or improves on the more complex optimizers.

The paper also presents an analysis suggesting that many specialized multi-task optimizers can partly be understood as regularization methods. That interpretation could help explain why familiar regularization techniques make the simple approach competitive. The findings motivate reevaluating the contribution of optimizer complexity in these settings and treating a carefully configured summed-loss approach as a serious comparison point when assessing multi-task learning methods.
neurips-2022-in-defense-of-the-unitary-s.tldr: Summing task losses with standard regularization matches or beats specialized multi-task optimizers in the settings studied.

paragraphs: A dataset can contain many measured coordinates while varying along far fewer underlying degrees of freedom. Intrinsic dimensionality estimates that smaller number. This paper addresses difficulties with nearest-neighbor approaches, whose computational cost grows quadratically with the number of samples and whose performance suffers when the data have many coordinates.

The proposed method uses normalizing flows and studies what happens when data are inflated with different amounts of noise. It examines singular values of the flow's Jacobian, quantities describing how the learned transformation changes different directions. The guiding calculations predict different behavior for directions tangent to the data manifold and directions normal to it.

That difference supplies a signal for estimating how many directions belong to the underlying data structure. The authors present the approach as scaling to both large datasets and high-dimensional observations. Tests include 64-by-64 RGB images and yield state-of-the-art results on the evaluated datasets. The contribution is to infer dimensionality from how a learned transformation responds to noise across directions.
neurips-2022-intrinsic-dimensionality-es.tldr: The method estimates intrinsic dimensionality by measuring how normalizing-flow Jacobians respond to different amounts of added noise.

paragraphs: This paper proposes adding a reflection stage to a neural network's decision process. The first stage is ordinary feed-forward inference, which associates the input with learned patterns. The second, slower stage considers the available choices and uses additional information to reassess the decision. The authors call the combined process introspective learning.

Reflection is implemented through gradients extracted from trained networks. A three-layer multilayer perceptron uses these gradient features to make the second-stage prediction. The paper also visualizes post-hoc explanations from both stages, giving a perceptual view of how the proposed reflection relates to the initial feed-forward decision.

For recognition on noisy data, the authors report 4% greater robustness and 42% less susceptibility to calibration errors. They also illustrate applications to active learning, out-of-distribution detection, and uncertainty estimation, where generalization and confidence quality matter. An image-quality assessment application connects the proposal to human introspection. The technical contribution is a concrete two-stage predictor that turns gradient information into an additional basis for decision making.
neurips-2022-introspective-learning-a-tw.tldr: Introspective learning adds a gradient-based reflection stage that improves reported robustness and calibration when recognizing noisy data.

paragraphs: Computing averages under a complicated probability distribution can be difficult when its normalization constant is unknown. This paper develops non-equilibrium importance sampling to estimate both expectations and normalization constants. It begins with samples from a simple distribution and moves them along paths generated by a velocity field.

The estimator averages along these paths, making the choice of velocity field central to its performance. The theoretical analysis explains how the field can be tailored to the target distribution and establishes conditions under which the estimator has zero variance. It also connects the method to approaches that transport a simple distribution onto a target through a mapping.

For computation, the authors represent the velocity field with a neural network and train it toward the zero-variance optimum. On benchmark examples with dimensions up to ten, training reduces estimator variance by as much as six orders of magnitude compared with a vanilla estimator. The paper also compares against annealed importance sampling. These experiments illustrate substantial possible gains, while zero variance remains tied to the stated theoretical conditions.
neurips-2022-learning-optimal-flows-for-.tldr: Learned velocity fields guide non-equilibrium importance sampling toward lower variance, with zero variance established under specified conditions.

paragraphs: Fixed-budget best-arm identification asks how to use a limited number of observations to select the best option. This paper studies that problem in linear bandits, where the options share a linear structure. The aim is to control the probability of choosing incorrectly after the observation budget has been spent.

The proposed parameter-free algorithm, OD-LinBAI, incorporates G-optimal experimental design into its allocation rule. Its failure-probability analysis depends on the optimality gaps of only the top d arms, where d is the instance's effective dimension. This identifies a dependence on a particular subset of competitive options rather than requiring the gaps of every arm.

The authors also derive a minimax lower bound describing the problem's worst-case difficulty. Together, their upper and lower bounds establish minimax optimality up to constant multiplicative factors in the exponent. Numerical experiments on real and synthetic datasets show considerable improvements over existing algorithms. The contribution combines a concrete allocation strategy with a tightly qualified optimality result and empirical evidence of its effectiveness.
neurips-2022-minimax-optimal-fixed-budge.tldr: OD-LinBAI uses optimal experimental design to identify the best linear-bandit arm with minimax guarantees up to constant factors in the exponent.

paragraphs: Predicting a tree-shaped output arises in dependency parsing, where a model identifies relationships between words. Standard likelihood or margin objectives may not align with the loss used to evaluate those predictions. Directly minimizing risk addresses that mismatch but typically creates a non-convex optimization problem.

This paper proposes a distributionally robust objective based on moments. It considers a set of distributions whose moment divergence from the empirical distribution is bounded, then minimizes the worst-case expected loss within that set. This puts uncertainty about the data distribution directly into the learning objective and connects training to the evaluation loss.

The authors develop efficient algorithms for arborescences and other tree variants. They also derive Fisher consistency, convergence rates, and generalization bounds, supplying theoretical support for the proposed learning procedure. Empirical evaluation uses dependency parsing benchmarks. The contribution brings together a loss-aware objective, an explicit distributional uncertainty formulation, and algorithms specialized to tree outputs, providing a structured approach to the mismatch between training objectives and evaluation.
neurips-2022-moment-distributionally-rob.tldr: The method learns tree predictions by minimizing worst-case expected loss over distributions constrained by their moment divergence from observed data.

paragraphs: Structure-based drug design searches for molecules that bind strongly to a target protein. Genetic algorithms can optimize molecular candidates effectively, but their design steps may explore randomly without using the protein's structure. This paper adds learned guidance to that search through a Reinforced Genetic Algorithm, or RGA.

Neural models take the three-dimensional structures of targets and ligands as inputs and prioritize promising design steps. They are first trained on native complex structures to draw on binding knowledge shared across targets, then fine-tuned during optimization. The aim is to suppress random-walk behavior while retaining the genetic algorithm's molecular optimization process.

Across the disease targets studied, RGA outperforms the evaluated baselines on docking scores and is more robust to random initialization. An ablation study also indicates that training across different targets improves performance, supporting the usefulness of shared binding information. The stated evidence concerns computational binding optimization: the method combines structure-informed guidance with search and demonstrates gains in the docking-based evaluations reported.
neurips-2022-reinforced-genetic-algorith.tldr: RGA uses neural guidance from protein and ligand structures to improve genetic search for molecules on docking-based evaluations.

paragraphs: Monte-Carlo tree search can improve decisions by exploring possible future actions, but that exploration can consume substantial time. This paper asks how to spend search computation more selectively. Its proposed variant, Virtual MCTS, adapts the amount of search to the difficulty of the state being considered.

The guiding idea is to devote more time to harder states and less to simpler ones. This makes the allocation of computation part of the search method itself. The authors provide theoretical bounds for their approach and evaluate both decision performance and computational cost, keeping the quality of the resulting actions alongside the time required to choose them.

Experiments use 9-by-9 Go and Atari games. In these evaluations, Virtual MCTS achieves performance comparable to the original search algorithm while using less than half its search time on average. The average-time qualification matters: the method deliberately varies effort across states. These results support adaptive search allocation as a viable approach for tasks with limited computation or decision time.
neurips-2022-spending-thinking-time-wise.tldr: Virtual MCTS allocates search time by state difficulty, retaining comparable game performance with less than half the average search time in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Showing that a neural network can represent a function does not by itself establish that the function can be learned statistically. Some approximation constructions depend on unrealistic features such as infinite numerical precision. This paper introduces a definition of statistically meaningful approximation that also requires good statistical learnability.

The authors study Boolean circuits and time-bounded Turing machines. For Boolean circuits, they show that overparameterized feed-forward networks can provide meaningful approximations with sample complexity polynomial in circuit size, independent of the approximating network's size. The guarantee therefore connects the needed data to the target computation rather than the potentially much larger network.

For Turing machines with computation time bounded by T, transformers achieve sample complexity polynomial in alphabet size, state-space size, and log(T). The analysis introduces tools for generalization bounds that yield much tighter guarantees than typical VC-dimension or norm-based bounds in these studies. The contribution strengthens expressivity analysis by asking whether an approximating construction also comes with favorable guarantees about how much data learning requires.
neurips-2022-statistically-meaningful-ap.tldr: The paper strengthens neural approximation theory with learnability requirements and derives sample-complexity guarantees for circuits and time-bounded Turing machines.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks often produce representations that are reused across several prediction tasks. An explanation method trained for one specific task can be difficult to reuse in that setting. The problem is especially relevant when a graph encoder is trained without supervision and its eventual downstream tasks are not yet known.

TAGE addresses this by learning an explainer through self-supervision without knowledge of downstream tasks. Its training is independent of the downstream prediction models. This allows the same explainer to support graph embedding models used for previously unseen tasks and to explain predictions from multitask models more efficiently.

Experiments show significant gains in explanation efficiency from reusing one model across multiple downstream tasks. Explanation quality is as good as, or better than, the state-of-the-art approaches evaluated. The contribution is therefore both a broader training setup for graph explanations and an empirical efficiency benefit: learning an explainer before the downstream tasks are specified can still support useful explanations when those tasks arrive.
neurips-2022-task-agnostic-graph-explana.tldr: TAGE learns a self-supervised graph explainer that can be reused across downstream tasks, improving efficiency while maintaining strong explanation quality.

paragraphs: Training a transformer requires retaining intermediate activations for the backward pass. These stored values can fill accelerator memory and restrict batch size. Because larger batches can potentially improve throughput, memory consumption can limit training speed even when the main issue appears to be computational cost.

Tempo reduces this memory burden through drop-in replacements for GELU, LayerNorm, and Attention layers. The approach targets commonly used transformer components so that their memory use becomes more efficient during training. The resulting capacity can support larger batches, linking a change in how layers use memory to improved overall training throughput.

The authors evaluate memory use, throughput, and accuracy or loss during BERT Large pretraining. Tempo enables batch sizes up to twice as large and achieves 16% higher throughput than the stated baseline. Evaluations on GPT2 and RoBERTa report speedups of 19% and 26%, respectively. These measurements demonstrate that reducing stored training data within transformer layers can translate into practical performance gains on the evaluated models.
neurips-2022-tempo-accelerating-transfor.tldr: Tempo reduces transformer-layer memory use, enabling larger batches and faster training on BERT Large, GPT2, and RoBERTa.

paragraphs: Virtual try-on deforms a three-dimensional garment representation to fit a target body. Combining several garments introduces another problem: the layers must interact without their surfaces colliding. This paper studies that challenge for neural fields, focusing on the complexity created when different garments are mixed and matched.

ULNeF proposes a neural model that untangles layered fields to represent collision-free garment surfaces. Its central component is a neural projection operator applied directly to the layered neural fields. Handling the interaction at this level avoids making an explicit surface representation the object on which the untangling operation must work.

The distinction matters because the paper identifies interactions between layers as a fundamental challenge for existing neural-field methods. Its contribution is a mechanism for addressing those interactions within the implicit representation itself, extending the approach beyond a single garment layer. The authors further argue that direct operations on neural representations could enable substantially different approaches to object interaction, presenting that broader impact as a possibility opened by the method.
neurips-2022-ulnef-untangled-layered-neu.tldr: ULNeF untangles layered neural fields directly to represent collision-free garments for mix-and-match virtual try-on.
